generated_output.summary: When a command line association or custom `get_command` hook invokes `ctx.fail()` during command resolution or completion (such as bash completion), Click raises a `UsageError`. However, if this occurs outside of the standard standalone execution block or during certain resolution routines where the exception isn't caught and handled cleanly via `ClickException.show()` and `sys.exit()`, an unhandled exception traceback is printed instead of a clean user-facing error message.
generated_output.root_cause_analysis: Functions like `ctx.fail()` raise `UsageError`, which inherits from `ClickException`. In standard command invocation via `Command.main()`, these are caught and handled by printing `.show()` and calling `sys.exit(e.exit_code)`. However, during auxiliary flows like shell completion (e.g. `_bashcomplete` or `_resolve_context`) or custom callback hooks where `standalone_mode` or exception handling blocks are bypassed or not active, the exception bubbles up uncaught, leading to a raw Python traceback.

step_by_step_plan.description: Examine the exception handling logic in src/click/core.py -> Command.main to understand how ClickException and UsageError are caught during standard execution.

step_by_step_plan.title: Examine shell completion and resolution hooks
step_by_step_plan.description: Inspect how command resolution and shell completion routines (such as completion script handlers and _resolve_context) invoke custom callbacks and get_command hooks without standalone exception boundaries.

step_by_step_plan.title: Wrap auxiliary invocation entrypoints with proper ClickException handling
step_by_step_plan.description: Ensure that custom get_command hooks, completion handlers, and context resolution steps catch UsageError / ClickException gracefully, invoking show() and exiting with the correct exit code instead of raising unhandled tracebacks.

step_by_step_plan.title: Add regression test for ctx.fail in custom get_command hooks
step_by_step_plan.description: Add a new test case in the test suite that simulates shell completion or command resolution triggering a custom get_command hook which calls ctx.fail(), asserting that a clean usage error message and correct exit status are produced rather than a traceback.

step_by_step_plan.title: Run pytest to verify regression tests pass
step_by_step_plan.description: Execute pytest to verify that the fix correctly addresses the unhandled exception during command resolution and that all existing tests continue to pass.

structured_concepts.short_explanation: Catching domain-specific user errors and converting them into clean terminal messages rather than crashing with a programming traceback.
structured_concepts.why_it_matters: End users should never see Python tracebacks for invalid inputs or configuration errors; they need clear, actionable error messages.
structured_concepts.connection_to_issue: The issue occurs because a `UsageError` raised during command resolution escapes its clean handler and bubbles up as an unhandled exception.

structured_concepts.short_explanation: The relationship between `ClickException`, `UsageError`, and standard Python exceptions in Click.
structured_concepts.why_it_matters: Click uses specialized exception classes to differentiate between user usage errors (exit code 2) and internal bugs (exit code 1 or unhandled tracebacks).
structured_concepts.connection_to_issue: `ctx.fail()` raises `UsageError`, which is designed to be caught and displayed gracefully by Click's top-level runners.

common_pitfalls: Modifying exception classes globally without checking how different entry points (like shell completion and testing runners) handle exceptions.
Catching generic `Exception` blocks which might mask actual programming bugs.
